message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average; 1.00794 u for protium) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (^2H or D, 0.02 %) – stable; Tritium (^3H or T, 0.0001 %) – radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 yr) |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (negative, meaning it releases energy when gaining an electron) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) at 1 atm |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) at 1 atm |
| **Density** | 0.08988 g cm⁻³ at 25 °C (liquid: 0.0708 g cm⁻³ at 20 °C) |
| **Molar volume** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ (ideal gas at STP) |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas (diatomic H₂) |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (range 4–75 % by volume) |
| **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂); reacts with halogens (forming HX) and oxygen (forming H₂O) under suitable conditions |
| **Bonding** | Covalent (H₂), ionic (metal hydrides), polar covalent (hydroxyl groups) |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – key in astrophysics |
| **Applications** | Fuel cell technology, rocket propellant (LH₂/LOX), industrial hydrogenation, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), medical imaging (MRI contrast agents), semiconductor manufacturing, etc. |
| **Safety notes** | Highly explosive with air; leaks can form invisible, odorless clouds; requires proper ventilation and leak detection systems |

---

### Quick Reference Cheat Sheet

| Category | Typical Values |
|----------|----------------|
| **Physical** | Boiling point –253 °C, Melting point –259 °C, Density 0.09 g cm⁻³ |
| **Chemical** | Diatomic (H₂), electronegativity 2.20, ionization energy 13.6 eV |
| **Isotopic** | Protium (stable), Deuterium (stable), Tritium (radioactive) |
| **Industrial** | Fuel cells, rocket fuel, ammonia production, metal hydrides |
| **Safety** | Flammable, explosive range 4–75 %, invisible, odorless |

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
